Answer ALL ten questions: the eight questions of Section A (Pure Mathematics, 66 marks) and the two questions of Section B (Mechanics, 17 marks each). In the examination itself, candidates answer all of Section A and any two questions from EITHER Section B (Mechanics) OR Section C (Statistics and Probability), never a mixture of B and C; this original paper contains only Section A and Section B. questions.enonce_markdown: The polynomial $f(x)=x^{3}+kx^{2}-4x-12$ has $(x-2)$ as a factor. Find the value of the constant $k$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
If $(x-a)$ is a factor of $f(x)$ then $f(a)=0$.

Since $(x-2)$ is a factor, $f(2)=0$: $2^{3}+k(2)^{2}-4(2)-12=8+4k-8-12=4k-12=0$, so $k=3$.

**Answer: $k=3$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: With this value of $k$, factorise $f(x)$ completely.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Divide the cubic by the known linear factor to obtain a quadratic, then factorise the quadratic.

$f(x)=x^{3}+3x^{2}-4x-12=x^{2}(x+3)-4(x+3)=(x+3)(x^{2}-4)=(x+3)(x-2)(x+2)$. Check: $f(-2)=-8+12+8-12=0$ and $f(-3)=-27+27+12-12=0$.

**Answer: $(x-2)(x+2)(x+3)$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The roots of the equation $2x^{2}-6x+3=0$ are $\alpha$ and $\beta$. State the values of $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
For $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$: $\alpha+\beta=-\dfrac{b}{a}$ and $\alpha\beta=\dfrac{c}{a}$.

$a=2$, $b=-6$, $c=3$, so $\alpha+\beta=-\dfrac{-6}{2}=3$ and $\alpha\beta=\dfrac{3}{2}$.

**Answer: $\alpha+\beta=3$, $\alpha\beta=\dfrac{3}{2}$.**

rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: For $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$: $\alpha+\beta=-\dfrac{b}{a}$ and $\alpha\beta=\dfrac{c}{a}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: For the same equation, find a quadratic equation, with integer coefficients, whose roots are $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}$ and $\dfrac{1}{\beta}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
A quadratic with roots $p$ and $q$ is $x^{2}-(p+q)x+pq=0$. Find the sum and the product of the new roots from $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$.

Sum of the new roots: $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}+\dfrac{1}{\beta}=\dfrac{\beta+\alpha}{\alpha\beta}=\dfrac{3}{\frac{3}{2}}=2$. Product: $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}\times\dfrac{1}{\beta}=\dfrac{1}{\alpha\beta}=\dfrac{2}{3}$. The equation is $x^{2}-2x+\dfrac{2}{3}=0$; multiplying by $3$ gives $3x^{2}-6x+2=0$.

**Answer: $3x^{2}-6x+2=0$.**

### Piège à éviter
$\dfrac{1}{\alpha}+\dfrac{1}{\beta}$ is not $\dfrac{1}{\alpha+\beta}$: add the fractions over the common denominator $\alpha\beta$.

criteres_notation.libelle: You find the sum of the new roots: $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}+\dfrac{1}{\beta}=\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha\beta}=2$

questions.enonce_markdown: A committee of $6$ people is to be chosen from $7$ men and $5$ women. Find the number of committees that contain at least $4$ men.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
“At least” means that several cases are possible: count each case with combinations, multiply the choices within a case and add the cases.

There are three cases. $4$ men and $2$ women: $\dbinom{7}{4}\times\dbinom{5}{2}=35\times10=350$. $5$ men and $1$ woman: $\dbinom{7}{5}\times\dbinom{5}{1}=21\times5=105$. $6$ men and no woman: $\dbinom{7}{6}=7$. The total is $350+105+7=462$.

**Answer: $462$.**

### Piège à éviter
The choices inside one case are multiplied; the different cases are added.

criteres_notation.libelle: You identify the three cases: $4$ men and $2$ women, $5$ men and $1$ woman, $6$ men

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the term in $x^{3}$ in the expansion of $\left(2x+\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{7}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The general term of $(a+b)^{n}$ is $\dbinom{n}{r}a^{n-r}b^{r}$. Collect the powers of $x$ in the general term and solve for $r$.

General term: $T_{r+1}=\dbinom{7}{r}(2x)^{7-r}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{r}=\dbinom{7}{r}2^{7-r}x^{7-r}x^{-r}=\dbinom{7}{r}2^{7-r}x^{7-2r}$. For $x^{3}$: $7-2r=3$, so $r=2$. The term is $\dbinom{7}{2}2^{5}x^{3}=21\times32\,x^{3}=672x^{3}$.

**Answer: $672x^{3}$.**

### Piège à éviter
The factor $2$ belongs to $2x$ and is raised to the power $7-r=5$; the power of $x$ is $7-r-r$.

criteres_notation.libelle: You find the power of $x$: $x^{7-2r}$, so $7-2r=3$ and $r=2$

rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: The general term of $(a+b)^{n}$ is $\dbinom{n}{r}a^{n-r}b^{r}$. Collect the powers of $x$ in the general term and solve for $r$.

exercices.enonce_intro_markdown: A farmer plants trees in rows. The first row has $5$ trees and each row after it has $3$ more trees than the row before.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the number of trees in the $12^{\text{th}}$ row.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The numbers of trees form an arithmetic progression: $T_{n}=a+(n-1)d$.

$a=5$, $d=3$, so $T_{12}=5+(12-1)\times3=5+33=38$ trees.

**Answer: $38$.**

criteres_notation.libelle: You recognise an arithmetic progression with $a=5$ and $d=3$

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the total number of trees in the first $12$ rows.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression is $S_{n}=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$, where $l$ is the last term.

$S_{12}=\dfrac{12}{2}(5+38)=6\times43=258$ trees.

**Answer: $258$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The farmer wants a row to have more than $60$ trees. Find the number of the first row which does.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Write the condition as an inequality in $n$, solve it, then take the smallest whole number that satisfies it.

$5+3(n-1)>60$ gives $3(n-1)>55$, so $n-1>18.3$ and $n>19.3$. The first whole number is $n=20$. Check: $T_{20}=5+57=62>60$ and $T_{19}=5+54=59<60$.

**Answer: $20^{\text{th}}$ row.**

### Piège à éviter
The answer must be a whole number of rows: $19.3$ rows does not exist, and $n=19$ gives $59$ trees, not more than $60$.

| $*$ | 1 | 3 | 7 | 9 |

| **1** | 1 | 3 | | 9 |

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that $S$ forms a group under $*$. [Assume that $*$ is associative.]
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
A set with an operation is a group when it is closed, associative, has an identity element and every element has an inverse.

**Closure:** every entry in the table is $1$, $3$, $7$ or $9$, so $x*y\in S$ for all $x$ and $y$. **Identity:** the row of $1$ is $1,3,7,9$ and the column of $1$ is $1,3,7,9$, so $1$ is the identity. **Inverses:** $1*1=1$, $3*7=1$, $7*3=1$ and $9*9=1$, so $1^{-1}=1$, $3^{-1}=7$, $7^{-1}=3$, $9^{-1}=9$. Associativity is assumed. All the axioms hold, so $(S,*)$ is a group.

**Answer: $S$ is a group under $*$.**

### Piège à éviter
Check that the identity appears in every row: an element has an inverse only if $1$ appears in its row.

criteres_notation.libelle: Closure: every entry of the table belongs to $S$
Identity: $1$, because the row and the column of $1$ repeat the headings
Inverses: $1^{-1}=1$, $3^{-1}=7$, $7^{-1}=3$ and $9^{-1}=9$, each found by locating $1$ in the table
You conclude that $S$ is a group under $*$

rappels_de_methode.competence: Binary Operations and Groups: Identity, Inverse and Tables
rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: A set with an operation is a group when it is closed, associative, has an identity element and every element has an inverse.

questions.enonce_markdown: A point $P$ is mapped to the point $(7,12)$ by the transformation $T:(x,y)\mapsto(3x+y,\ 5x+2y)$. Find the coordinates of $P$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
If $T$ is represented by $M$ and the image of $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}$ is $\begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$, then $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=M^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$.

$M=\begin{pmatrix}3&1\\5&2\end{pmatrix}$ with $\det M=3\times2-1\times5=1$, so $M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-5&3\end{pmatrix}$. Then $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-5&3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}7\\12\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}14-12\\-35+36\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\end{pmatrix}$. Check: $T(2,1)=(6+1,\ 10+2)=(7,12)$.

**Answer: $(2,1)$.**

criteres_notation.libelle: You find the inverse: determinant $1$, inverse $\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-5&3\end{pmatrix}$

rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: If $T$ is represented by $M$ and the image of $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}$ is $\begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$, then $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=M^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$.

exercices.enonce_intro_markdown: A school buys $x$ bags of rice at $12000$ FCFA each and $y$ bags of beans at $9000$ FCFA each. The total cost must not exceed $132000$ FCFA, and the number of bags of rice must be at least twice the number of bags of beans.

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that $4x+3y\leq44$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Write the condition in words as an inequality, then divide by a common factor.

The cost of $x$ bags of rice and $y$ bags of beans is $12000x+9000y$ FCFA, and it is at most $132000$: $12000x+9000y\leq132000$. Dividing every term by $3000$ gives $4x+3y\leq44$.

rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: Write the condition in words as an inequality, then divide by a common factor.

questions.enonce_markdown: Write down another inequality, in terms of $x$ and $y$, which satisfies the condition on the number of bags.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
“At least twice” means greater than or equal to two times.

The number of bags of rice is at least twice the number of bags of beans: $x\geq2y$.

**Answer: $x\geq2y$.**

rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: “At least twice” means greater than or equal to two times.

questions.enonce_markdown: On graph paper, taking $1$ cm to represent $1$ unit on both axes, draw the lines $4x+3y=44$ and $x=2y$, and shade the region $R$ in which all the conditions are satisfied. (Remember that $x\geq0$ and $y\geq0$.)
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Draw each boundary line from two points, then test a point to decide which side satisfies each inequality. The region satisfying all the inequalities lies on the correct side of every line.

$4x+3y=44$ passes through $(11,0)$ and $(5,8)$. $x=2y$ passes through $(0,0)$ and $(8,4)$. Test $(5,1)$: $4(5)+3(1)=23\leq44$ and $5\geq2(1)$, so the region contains $(5,1)$: it is the triangle below the line $4x+3y=44$, below the line $x=2y$ and above the $x$-axis. The lines meet at $(8,4)$, because $4(2y)+3y=44$ gives $y=4$ and $x=8$.

questions.enonce_markdown: The lines intersect. Find the values of the parameters $s$ and $t$ at the point of intersection.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
At the point of intersection the two position vectors are equal: equate the $\mathbf{i}$-components and the $\mathbf{j}$-components to get two simultaneous equations in $s$ and $t$.

$2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+s(\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})=-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+t(5\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$. $\mathbf{i}$: $2+s=-1+5t$, so $s=5t-3$. $\mathbf{j}$: $1+3s=3+4t$. Substituting: $1+3(5t-3)=3+4t$, so $15t-8=3+4t$, $11t=11$ and $t=1$. Then $s=5(1)-3=2$.

**Answer: $s=2$ and $t=1$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $y=x^{2}\sqrt{1+2x}$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, simplifying your answer.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The product rule: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(uv)=u\dfrac{dv}{dx}+v\dfrac{du}{dx}$; the chain rule gives $\dfrac{d}{dx}(1+2x)^{\frac{1}{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2}(1+2x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\times2$.

$u=x^{2}$, $\dfrac{du}{dx}=2x$; $v=(1+2x)^{\frac{1}{2}}$, $\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2}(1+2x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\times2=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+2x}}$. $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^{2}\times\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+2x}}+\sqrt{1+2x}\times2x=\dfrac{x^{2}+2x(1+2x)}{\sqrt{1+2x}}=\dfrac{5x^{2}+2x}{\sqrt{1+2x}}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{5x^{2}+2x}{\sqrt{1+2x}}$.**

### Piège à éviter
The derivative of the bracket $2$ is a factor of the chain rule: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(1+2x)^{\frac{1}{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2}(1+2x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\times2$, not $\dfrac{1}{2}(1+2x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.

You differentiate $v$ by the chain rule: $\dfrac{dv}{dx}=(1+2x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$

questions.enonce_markdown: Two particles $P$ and $Q$ move in the plane of the coordinate axes $Ox$ and $Oy$. At time $t$ seconds, the position vectors of $P$ and $Q$, relative to the origin $O$, are $\left(2t^{2}\mathbf{i}+6t\mathbf{j}\right)$ m and $\left((t+4)\mathbf{i}-t^{2}\mathbf{j}\right)$ m respectively. Find the velocity of $P$ when $t=2$, and the speed of $P$ at that instant.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The velocity is the derivative of the position vector with respect to time; the speed is the magnitude of the velocity.

$\mathbf{r}_{P}=2t^{2}\mathbf{i}+6t\mathbf{j}$, so $\mathbf{v}_{P}=\dfrac{d\mathbf{r}_{P}}{dt}=4t\,\mathbf{i}+6\,\mathbf{j}$. At $t=2$: $\mathbf{v}_{P}=8\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The speed is $|\mathbf{v}_{P}|=\sqrt{8^{2}+6^{2}}=\sqrt{100}=10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

**Answer: $8\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.**

criteres_notation.libelle: You find the speed $\sqrt{8^{2}+6^{2}}=10$ m s$^{-1}$

rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: The velocity is the derivative of the position vector with respect to time; the speed is the magnitude of the velocity.

questions.enonce_markdown: For the same particles, calculate the velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ when $t=2$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ is $\mathbf{v}_{P}-\mathbf{v}_{Q}$: the velocity of $P$ minus the velocity of $Q$.

$\mathbf{r}_{Q}=(t+4)\mathbf{i}-t^{2}\mathbf{j}$, so $\mathbf{v}_{Q}=\mathbf{i}-2t\,\mathbf{j}$ and, at $t=2$, $\mathbf{v}_{Q}=\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}$. Then $\mathbf{v}_{P/Q}=(8\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})-(\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})=7\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

**Answer: $7\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.**

### Piège à éviter
Subtract the velocity of $Q$ from the velocity of $P$, in this order: $\mathbf{v}_{Q}-\mathbf{v}_{P}$ is the velocity of $Q$ relative to $P$.

criteres_notation.libelle: You differentiate the position vector of $Q$: $\mathbf{v}_{Q}=\mathbf{i}-2t\,\mathbf{j}$

rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: The velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ is $\mathbf{v}_{P}-\mathbf{v}_{Q}$: the velocity of $P$ minus the velocity of $Q$.

questions.enonce_markdown: A particle $A$ of mass $3$ kg and a particle $B$ of mass $5$ kg move in the same direction along a smooth horizontal straight line, with speeds $8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ respectively, $A$ being behind $B$. They collide. After the collision $A$ continues in the same direction at $3\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Find the speed of $B$ after the collision.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
In a collision on a smooth line, the total momentum is conserved: $m_{1}u_{1}+m_{2}u_{2}=m_{1}v_{1}+m_{2}v_{2}$.

Momentum before: $3\times8+5\times2=34$. Momentum after: $3\times3+5v=9+5v$. So $9+5v=34$, $5v=25$ and $v=5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

**Answer: $5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.**

### Rappel de méthode
The kinetic energy of a particle is $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$. The loss is the total before minus the total after.

Before: $\dfrac{1}{2}(3)(8)^{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}(5)(2)^{2}=96+10=106\ \text{J}$. After: $\dfrac{1}{2}(3)(3)^{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}(5)(5)^{2}=13.5+62.5=76\ \text{J}$. Loss $=106-76=30\ \text{J}$.

**Answer: $30\ \text{J}$.**

The resultant of several forces is their vector sum: add the $\mathbf{i}$-components together and the $\mathbf{j}$-components together.
